explanation: An 'ordinary lower/mixed-case English running text' dial whose strongest peaks (>0.6 of max) fall on a frequency/polarity/degree adverb (never, ever, once, often, sometimes, always, most) and on the one or two words right after it, typically a quantifier, determiner, particle or participle ('never any', 'has ever seen any', 'sometimes some', 'ever come across', 'most well-known'), with weaker peaks (0.25-0.55 of max) on 'one of', 'had no' and on ordinary English content words from the second word on, so most English sentences of four or more words reach about 0.3 of max. It is ~0 on the first token, on sentence-final periods and on all non-English text (French, German, Spanish, Italian, Dutch, Russian, CJK, lorem ipsum). It stays below ~0.25 of max on most ALL-CAPS English, on one-to-three-word greetings and labels ('Good morning', 'Best regards', 'Hi there'), on repeated or single-letter strings and on short code lines with no English words. After a non-English prefix the next English words stay weak; only an adverb+quantifier pair such as 'never any' climbs back to ~0.5 of max.
